summary: We have develop a web based app that monitors an astronauts condition such as their aerobic capacity, blood oxygen and even mental health. This app makes it easier for astronauts to track their health and take appropriate action to take care of their health to ensure their mission goes well. This app is important as it can provide astronauts with medical advice and diet plans even when communication with earth is down. This app will help astronauts to do their job more effectively while maintaining a healthy lifestyle even in space.
details:
How it works

Physical condition: The user will be able to choose on where they currently are such as in space, the moon or mars. This will affect the calculation as each location has different environmental properties. Then the user will input the data into the website according to the data received from their measuring tools. This data will then be calculated and compared to other verified data to see if the user is healthy or not. If user is in poor health, approved advice from NASA’s medical protocol will be provided according to the user’s needs. The user may also review their overall score for each data type and view past medical records and compare it with each other.

Mental Health: In order to measure the user’s mental health we will provide them with a GHQ-28 type based questionnaire as this questionnaire has been approved to measure mental health conditions such as depression, insomnia and anxiety. Their overall score will be provided and  depending on the severity of their mental health counselling advice will be provided.

Benefits and Impact

Health awareness: The system can improve the awareness of the astronaut's condition by presenting health information in an organized and understandable form for them. This makes the astronauts to better understand their health status.

Cardiovascular monitoring: This tool tracks heart rate and blood pressure to help astronauts understand their cardiovascular condition in depth. By identifying abnormal readings and monitoring changes over time, to avoid potential cardiovascular problems and helps evaluate astronauts' heart health.

Radiation exposure monitoring: This tool records radiation dose rates and cumulative exposure levels to help astronauts understand their radiation exposure during space missions. This supports radiation awareness and helps medical teams evaluate exposure history when assessing astronaut health risks.

Sleep monitoring: Tracks sleep duration and quality to identify sleep deprivation, fatigue, and irregular sleep patterns.

Historical Health Records: Allows the system to review previous medical records and compare past and current measurements to identify changes in their health.

Nutrition and hydration: Tracks calorie intake, protein consumption, and water intake to help astronauts maintain proper nutrition and hydration.

Autonomous and lightweight operation: Runs on a lightweight, self-hosted server (~92.5 MB RAM) with built-in NASA medical protocols, ensuring astronauts receive immediate risk warnings and recovery advice even during deep-space communication delays.

Tools used to build the app


1. Coding Languages 

The AstrumCare system was developed using several programming languages: 

JavaScript (ES6+ / Node.js)  

  • Frontend (script.js): Handles the main functions of the system, including health data analysis, psychological assessment using the WHO GHQ-28 questionnaire, health charts, health recommendations, and user authentication. 
  • Backend (server.js): Manages user login, access permissions, and saving health assessment results. 

CSS3  

  • styles.css: Controls the website's appearance, including its dark theme, layouts, animations, colours, and mobile-friendly design. 

HTML5 & Inline SVG  

  • Used to build the eight website pages: Home, Results, Assessment, Admin, Regimen, Advisory, Questionnaire, and Login. 
  • SVG graphics are used to display visual health indicators and dashboard elements. 

SQL (SQLite) 

  • Used to store and manage user accounts, login information, health assessment results, and historical health records. 

Bash / Shell Scripting 

  • Used on Ubuntu Linux to manage the server, install software, run commands, and automate deployment tasks. 

2. Software, Tools and Libraries 

The following software and tools were used to develop and operate AstrumCare: 

  • Node.js: Runs the backend system and handles server-side operations. 
  • Express.js: Connects the frontend website with the backend through REST APIs. 
  • SQLite: Stores user accounts and health assessment data. 
  • better-sqlite3: Allows the application to communicate with the SQLite database. 
  • bcryptjs: Protects user passwords by securely hashing them. 
  • PM2: Keeps the AstrumCare server running in the background. 
  • Git and GitHub: Used to manage and store the project's source code. 
  • SSH: Allows remote access to the Ubuntu server for development and maintenance. 
  • Web Storage API (sessionStorage): Stores temporary session and simulation data in the browser. 
  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Used as the main code editor for writing, editing, debugging, and managing the AstrumCare project's source code. 

3. Hardware and Hosting Infrastructure 

  • Server: AstrumCare is hosted on our own dedicated HP Slim Desktop S01 server, running Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (64-bit). This allows us to host and manage the system ourselves. 
  • Server Specifications: The server is equipped with an Intel Core i5-9400 6-core processor, 32 GB RAM and a 500 GB SSD. AstrumCare is designed to be lightweight, using only around 20 MB of storage and approximately 92.5 MB of RAM while running.  
  • Network & Domain: The server is connected to the internet through a wired Ethernet connection. We use our custom domain, astrumcare.panamis.my, with Cloudflare Dynamic DNS (DDNS) to automatically update the server's public IP address every five minutes. This helps keep the website accessible even when the public IP address changes. 
  • Development & Testing: The system was developed using a Windows computer and remotely managed through SSH. 

App Specialty

In Astrum Care, not only do we monitor the user’s health in space but also in all 3 major environment which is in space, the moon and mars. The app would give them advice and steps they should take to recover as well as some risk they are exposed too . AstrumCare also shows a diet and workout plan to the user so they may follow the diet plan provided to take better care of themselves. So not only can the user monitor their own health with AstrumCare but also provide the necessary advice and counseling as if it was a mobile doctor.

Factors Considered

Our team has considered six main factors when developing AstrumCare.

First, we have considered the different environment astronauts gonna be in, which is around the orbit(space), on the moon and on Mars.

Secondly, we have considered their individual biometrics such as age, height and mass, and many other data values (up to 13) then will be processed by our formulas in our website to calculate the risk and give advise according to it.

Thirdly, we have thought about not only the physical health of the astronaut, but also the mental health of the astronaut. We evaluate the astronauts physical health through the 13 data values that they key in. As for the mental health of the astronauts, we evaluate it through the clinical GHQ-28 psychological screen.

And lastly, we have considered all the actions (that we possibly could) that could mitigate the common risk by translating abnormal telemetry into 13 NASA-STD-3001 risk warnings and hardware-specific (ARED/CEVIS/T2) diet and workout regimens.
